text:
The site theme is deliberately CSS-only: everything lives in static/custom.css, which mdBook loads after its own stylesheets via additional-css.

Overriding mdBook's Handlebars templates (a theme/ directory with index.hbs) was considered and rejected. It would give full control over the DOM, but it makes every future mdBook upgrade a merge against upstream templates. mdBook 0.5 exposes enough CSS custom properties (in its css/variables.css) to do a complete restyle without touching templates, so upgrades stay routine. Adding JavaScript was ruled out for the same reason. Both constraints survived the second restyle in Aug 2026.

Consequences worth knowing before trying to change the design:
- The sidebar renders inside an iframe (toc.html) when JavaScript is off, and as an inline custom element when it is on. custom.css IS loaded in the iframe document so styling works, but no CSS selector can span the parent page and the sidebar, and any sidebar rule has to look right in both shapes.
- mdBook's prev/next anchors are icon-only, with no chapter title in the markup, so 'Previous: Some Chapter' is not reachable without a template override or JS. Rather than add JS, the whole feature was removed. See the separate navigation entry.
- mdBook has five theme classes (light/rust/coal/navy/ayu). Rather than style two and hide the rest, all five are mapped onto two palettes: light+rust to light, coal+navy+ayu to dark. This is what makes it safe to hide the theme picker, because a visitor with a stale theme choice in localStorage can still never land on an unstyled page.
- The theme class stays on <html> when printing, so the @media print block has to reset the design's own token layer (--paper/--ink/--rule and the hardcoded syntax colours), not just mdBook's --bg and --fg. Overriding only mdBook's variables prints near-white text on white paper for anyone using a dark theme.

move_html_to_dir rewrites page.html to page/index.html for prettier URLs, which adds one directory level AFTER mdBook has already computed its asset paths relative to the original page depth. Any relative path mdBook emits is therefore wrong in the built output.

This has bitten three times. build already had a sed for path_to_root. In Aug 2026 we found path_to_searchindex_js had the same problem, which meant search was silently dead on every note page of the live site (only the root page worked). The request resolved to a sibling directory and the host returned another page's HTML with a 200 and content-type text/html, so the script failed to parse with no visible error. Later the same month we found mdBook's toc.js compares link.href against a current_page it has appended index.html to, which never matches a trailing-slash note URL, so the sidebar highlight and the on-this-page list were both dead.

Rule for anything added later: asset URLs authored by us must be root-absolute (/fonts/x.woff2, not ../fonts/x.woff2), and any new relative path or URL comparison mdBook emits into the built output needs a corresponding rewrite in build. This is also why 'mdbook serve' is NOT the preview command - it skips move_html_to_dir and the sed passes entirely, so it hides exactly this class of bug. Use .symphony/serve, which runs the real pipeline.

Note on hosting, because an earlier version of this entry got it wrong: the site is served by Cloudflare Pages, building from the GitHub repository. Stavros confirmed in Aug 2026 that nothing has ever talked to GitLab and that he does not use it. The stale gitlab.com URL in book.toml, the fab-gitlab icon and the 'upload it to GitLab pages' copy were all leftovers and have been removed. The remaining gitlab.com links in content/ are genuine links to his own projects (Parachute, esp32-cnc, assault-and-battery) and are unrelated to deployment.

The emoji prefixes that joplinexport used to write into content/SUMMARY.md link text (a document glyph on every note, the Joplin folder emoji or a folder glyph on every folder) were removed deliberately in Aug 2026, as part of the restyle. Reasons: 60-odd identical document glyphs dominated the sidebar and worked against the calm look; and entries where only some items carried a chosen emoji read as accidental rather than intentional. Sidebar hierarchy is now carried by CSS instead (weight for folders at any depth, indent guides, accent bar on the active item).

Removing them also fixed browser tab titles as a side effect, because mdBook derives <title> from the SUMMARY link text, so tabs used to read '<glyph> Some note - Stavros Notes'.

The Folder.icon field, the icon column in the folders SELECT, and the json.loads that decoded Joplin's icon JSON were all deleted as dead code at the same time. If folder icons are ever wanted again, that is where the data comes from.

Webfonts are loaded from the Google Fonts CDN, not self-hosted. This reverses the earlier decision (Aug 2026) to self-host Source Serif 4 under static/fonts/ with a ~150KB budget; those files were deleted when the design changed.

Stavros chose the CDN explicitly when told the tradeoff: self-hosting the three families the new design needs (Newsreader for body, Public Sans for headings and UI, JetBrains Mono for code and labels) would have been roughly 250-350KB of woff2, versus a third-party request and a render-blocking @import for the CDN. He was not worried about the page weight or the third-party request.

So do not 'fix' the @import back to self-hosted files without asking. If it ever does come back, the OFL licence text has to come with it, and the URLs must be root-absolute for the reason recorded in the build-pipeline entry.

Prev/next navigation is deliberately removed, not merely unstyled. .nav-wrapper, .nav-wide-wrapper and .mobile-nav-chapters are all display:none in static/custom.css.

Stavros' reason, in his words: nobody is going to go from 'programming an F4 MCU' to 'soldering a clock board' as a natural continuation. These are notes, not a book, so there are no reading sequences and sequential navigation has nothing to offer.

This supersedes the earlier note that prev/next was 'left as arrows' because mdBook's icon-only anchors carry no chapter title. That problem is now moot. It also means the CSS-only, no-JavaScript constraint survived the Aug 2026 restyle: injecting chapter titles into prev/next was the only thing that would have required JS, and the feature was dropped instead.

FIXED in Aug 2026 by a fourth sed pass in ./build. Recorded here because the cause is not guessable from the fix, and because the fix is a patch to vendored code that will need re-deriving on the next mdBook upgrade.

The symptom was that the sidebar never highlighted the current page on a note page; it worked only on the six folder index pages. Confirmed empirically at the time (0 elements matching '#mdbook-sidebar .active' on a note page, 1 on a folder page).

Cause: mdBook 0.5.2's toc.js normalises only one side of its comparison. It appends 'index.html' to location.href when that ends in '/', then tests 'link.href === current_page'. move_html_to_dir rewrites note pages to trailing-slash URLs, so link.href stayed '/x/y/' while current_page became '/x/y/index.html' and the test never passed. Folder pages still matched because mdBook emits their href as 'x/index.html' already.

Two consequences, both now resolved: the accent-tinted active row was dead on 65 of 71 pages, and the 'on this page' heading list was never built at all, because toc.js early-returns when it finds no active link. That list had therefore never rendered, which meant it had also never been styled - fixing the highlight made a previously invisible piece of UI appear for the first time, and it needed styling in the same change.

The fix normalises both sides at comparison time only, as an inline expression, so the href attribute keeps the pretty /x/y/ URL. Do not be tempted to rewrite the href instead; that would undo the whole point of move_html_to_dir. It deliberately introduces no new variable binding, so that a future toc.js declaring the same name cannot collide and turn a cosmetic failure into a SyntaxError that kills the sidebar entirely.

Why the pass asserts exact occurrence counts before and after, rather than just substituting: this patches program logic in a vendored, hash-named file, so an upgrade could silently no-op or half-apply. Silent failure is exactly how the path_to_searchindex_js bug survived unnoticed on the live site. When mdBook is next upgraded, expect ./build to abort here and re-derive the pattern against the new toc.js.

Related, and left alone: a heading that is itself a markdown link produces an empty row in the on-this-page list. mdBook emits nested anchors, which are invalid HTML, so the parser un-nests them and toc.js copies only the now-empty a.header into the row. That is hidden in CSS rather than patched in JS. The no-JS sidebar path (the iframe at /toc/) has no active-link logic at all and inherently cannot have one.
